messages:
Priya Rao: Quick sync — AcmeCorp has locked on BYOK + regional data sovereignty. They want: retained audit evidence for 7 years, on-demand legal hold, and per-tenant exportability. Need us to confirm launch criteria by EOW.
Ben Kim: Are they asking for full plaintext audit logs or a proofable export (signed manifests)?
Carmen Li: They explicitly mentioned 'evidence' for audits. Likely want enough detail for SOC2 + legal discovery. We should clarify minimal fields.
Priya Rao: Good point. @Ben can you list minimal event schema we can commit to (fields + TTL)?
Ben Kim: Quick draft: {actor, action, resource_id, timestamp, request_id, model_id, decision_route, response_hash}. TTL per retention policy.
Mark O'Neill: Ops question — storing per-tenant encrypted artifacts when keys are BYOK is heavier. We need sizing estimate. Can we do manifest-only in our storage and let keystore hold the keys?
Carmen Li: Manifest-only reduces storage but may not satisfy legal if they need full transcript. Need to know which customers will insist on transcript retention.
LegalBot: From legal: for discovery, courts typically want full content. For SOC2 evidence, manifests + checksums are often OK if retention and chain-of-custody are demonstrable. We need explicit customer contract language for partial-extract vs full-content retention.
Priya Rao: Action items: 1) Engineering to propose schema + storage tradeoffs; 2) Security/Ops to produce capacity and cost delta for manifest-only vs full-content; 3) Legal to supply contract language options. All by Thursday.
Ben Kim: On schema: adding response_hash lets us avoid storing PII-heavy content while enabling verification. We could also support encrypted snapshots stored in object store with customer KEK if they opt-in.
Mark O'Neill: That approach works. Two launch modes: "manifest-only" (default) and "snapshot-on-demand" (premium) where snapshot is encrypted with customer key and retained per SLA. Snapshot-on-demand requires a retained key escrow policy for legal hold.
Carmen Li: How do we handle cross-region requests? AcmeCorp wants EU residency for EU customers, US for US.
Priya Rao: Routing policy: data-in-region by tenant tag. Need KMS/keystore region affinity plus the ability to export full evidence to a specified region on demand.
LegalBot: For legal hold: when hold is applied we must refuse deletion and preserve keys per contract. If customer manages keys (BYOK), we need a protocol to ensure we can produce data for lawful requests — OR contractually require key escrow for legal hold scenarios.
Ben Kim: Implementation note: support a "preserve" flag on snapshots. Pseudocode:
```
POST /evidence/snapshots
{ "tenant": "acme", "request_id": "r-123", "preserve": true, "kms_key": "projects/.../keys/acme" }
```
Response includes manifest + storage pointer.
Mark O'Neill: Runbook: if preserve + BYOK and customer refuses escrow, escalate to legal and mark feature gated. Ops will block retention deletion per contract only if escrow exists.
Carmen Li: UX: add onboarding checkbox for "enable preserved snapshots for legal hold" with note about escrow requirement. Also surface estimated monthly cost.
Priya Rao: Prioritization ask: This is a customer-critical enterprise deal. If Legal and Ops provide language and sizing by Thu, we can slot a minimal GA for pilot in 6 weeks (manifest-only + snapshot-on-demand gated behind escrow). Otherwise push to Q3.
LegalBot: I'll draft three contract clauses: (A) full preservation with escrow, (B) manifest-only warrant, (C) snapshot-on-demand with customer-managed key + escrow opt-in.
DevBot: FYI automated ticket created: INF-1421 (acme evidence retention + keystore scoping).
Ben Kim: One last technical constraint: for verifying response_hash over model outputs we need deterministic normalization. I'll add a small spec for canonicalization.
Priya Rao: Thanks — I'll consolidate and schedule a 30m call Fri AM to review legal language + ops numbers. If anyone can't make it, drop notes here. :calendar:
